title: Lets Eliminate the Bureaucracy Together
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that eliminating organizational red tape requires actively soliciting front-line input, because the people closest to the work already know exactly what's slowing them down. It cites Amazon's initiative that generated 1,500 employee suggestions and led to more than 450 process changes as proof the approach works at scale. The author lays out a three-step method: define precisely what kind of bureaucracy you're targeting, build a transparent process for reviewing suggestions, and replace eliminated processes with something more streamlined rather than leaving a gap. It closes with a Laurence Peter quote about bureaucracy outliving its usefulness.
points: Team members already know exactly which rules and processes are wasting their time, if leaders ask
Amazon's employee-suggestion initiative generated 1,500 recommendations and changed 450+ processes
Define specifically what kind of bureaucracy the organization wants eliminated before soliciting ideas
Replace eliminated processes with something more streamlined rather than leaving a vacuum
quotes: Team members experience unnecessary rules, outdated processes, and redundant layers of approvals all day long.
After the CEO requested team members to send in suggestions via email, the company received 1500 recommendations and used them to change more than 450 of their processes based on the feedback.
Describing exactly what suggestions the enterprise is looking to eliminate with examples prevents people from making wild recommendations
Lastly, in many cases, the eliminated process must be replaced by something else less burdensome and more streamlined.
Bureaucracy defends the status quo long past the time when the quo has lost its status.
